Let’s dive into Chapter 9: Helping Others Find Their Element.
You know, searching for your Element isn’t just a solo adventure. The people around you—parents, teachers, managers, or friends—can make a huge difference in helping you figure out what truly lights you up.
Sometimes, all it takes is asking the right question at the right moment. Or, maybe it’s a little encouragement when someone’s feeling uncertain.
Picture this: there’s a father who notices his daughter is completely fascinated by animals. Instead of nudging her toward something more “practical,” he takes her to the library to learn about wildlife. He even encourages her to volunteer at the local animal shelter. Fast forward a few years—she becomes a veterinarian, and she’s deeply grateful for that early support that let her follow her passion.
Teachers can have that same impact. Think about a student who struggles with math, but absolutely loves building things. One teacher suggests joining the robotics club. That simple nudge transforms the student’s attitude toward learning. Suddenly, he realizes he’s got a real knack for engineering.
Now, let’s talk about managers and leaders. They have a unique chance to shape an environment where people can use their strengths. Maybe a boss notices someone on the team is great at organizing events, and encourages them to take on new projects. Or maybe a team leader values creativity and actually sets aside time for the group to brainstorm and experiment—even if the results aren’t perfect every time.
Most of us don’t realize just how powerful a single act of encouragement can be. Sometimes, it’s as simple as a kind word, really listening, or seeing potential where everyone else only sees problems. That small gesture? It can honestly change the course of someone’s life.
Here’s something to pay attention to: challenging assumptions. Lots of people can’t see their own strengths, or maybe they’ve been told their interests aren’t valuable. Helping someone else find their Element means being willing to question those old beliefs, and offering support—even when the way forward isn’t obvious.
Think about communities where all kinds of talents and passions are welcomed. Those places are more vibrant and resilient, right? They give people space to try new things, to fail and give it another shot, and to celebrate each other’s wins—no matter how big or small.
So, what’s the real secret here? Helping others find their Element isn’t about pushing them in a specific direction. It’s about listening, encouraging them to explore, and trusting that everyone’s got something unique to bring to the table.
And the reward? It’s a world where more people feel alive, engaged, and ready to make a difference in ways that truly matter.
